# CANDIDATE: RSI_DIVERGENCE_LEVEL_BOUNCE

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Bullish (or bearish) RSI divergence at a named support/resistance level signals a reversal when price fails to make a new low/high. This edge exists because RSI divergence indicates weakening momentum, and named levels (prior day high/low, VWAP) often act as support/resistance, increasing reversal probability when combined with divergence.

## Mechanism

Entry rule: Identify a named level (prior day high/low, overnight VWAP, or session VWAP). For bullish: price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low and the low is within 0.1% of the support → enter long at the close of that bar. For bearish: price makes a higher high while RSI makes a lower high and the high is within 0.1% of the resistance → enter short at the close of that bar. Exit: Stop placed just beyond the named level (a few ticks below support for longs, above resistance for shorts); target 1.5R or use a chart‑stop at the next structural opposite (e.g., prior swing high for longs).
